clue.text: Old Pope, born in Britain, not in Germany, rejecting tea we hear, also fresh fruit after short holidays

indicators.note: something made fresh is renewed, so these letters come out in a new order
to reject something is to throw it out, so a letter is removed from the word before

parts.note: nicht is the German word for not

indicators.note: what we hear is what is said aloud, so a word is used for its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: the drink sounds like the letter T
taken as written, as anagram fodder
short holidays are breaks
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A potted biography of a medieval pope, oddly mixed with tea, fruit and holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Also' looks like a joining word but is fodder for the reshuffle. Adrian IV is the clue's subject, but the answer is his birth name, split across two entries.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Breakspear became Adrian IV in 1154, the only English-born man ever to be elected pontiff.

clue.text: See 1
Singer may not always be the same when losing voice at the start

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter drops out of the phrase
this pins down where the dropped letter sits: at the front of its word

parts.words: may not always be the same
parts.note: something that may not always be the same can vary
V is the grammatical abbreviation for voice, as in active and passive voice

explanation.surface: A performer whose voice is unreliable, sounding different from night to night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the start' says where the V goes: it is the first letter of VARY, not of the whole phrase. 'Singer' looks like a vocalist but is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The canary is a small finch famous for its song, so a bird is a singer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Union Jack raised by Reform MP after last of migrants will get what is fair

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters lifts the bottom one to the top, so the order flips

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for union
J is jack on playing cards

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: final letter of the word
Richard Tice is a Reform UK MP, the party's deputy leader

explanation.surface: A political scene: a populist MP waving the flag after talking about migrants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union Jack' looks like the British flag but is two abbreviations, U and J, turned upside down. Reform UK is a right-wing British party and Richard Tice one of its MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: Justice is fairness in treatment and judgement, so it is the quality of what is fair.

clue.text: For example Dutch PM, after consuming light meal, dismisses that person in education

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so some letters are removed from the name

parts.note: Dutch is an example of a tongue spoken in a country
afternoon tea is a light meal
Margaret Thatcher was a British Prime Minister
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Dutch prime minister eats a snack and then sacks someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch PM' looks like one person, but 'For example Dutch' is a whole piece and PM is a British prime minister. THATCHER, with TEA first, dismisses THAT to leave CHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who teaches a foreign tongue such as French or Dutch works in schools, so is a professional in teaching.

clue.text: Dry, only letting in a minimum of rain

indicators.note: to let something in is to admit it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'

indicators.note: the smallest possible amount of a word is a single letter, its first

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A drought-stricken place where barely any rain gets through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' reads as weather, but it describes wine. 'Only' meaning BUT is the older sense, as in 'he is but a boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut is the label for very dry sparkling wine, especially champagne, with little added sugar.

clue.text: Appropriate greeting to sailor

parts.note: an informal greeting
jack is an old word for a sailor, as in jack tar

explanation.surface: Etiquette advice on the right way to say hello to a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective meaning suitable, but it is the verb meaning to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack is to seize control of something belonging to another, the verb sense of appropriate.

clue.text: Range Rover's number one — for radio operators this car will be next

parts.note: surface reading: the top model of a luxury off-road vehicle

parts.words: for radio operators this car will be next
parts.note: setter's reading: Rover's first letter is R, called Romeo in the radio alphabet, and the letter after it has the name of a Ford model and of a mountain range

explanation.surface: A car buyer weighing up a Range Rover and the model they will buy next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range Rover' looks like the car brand, but 'Range' is one definition. In the NATO phonetic alphabet R is Romeo and the next letter is S, the same name as the Ford car.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged mountain chain, and the Ford Sierra was a popular British family saloon of the 1980s.

clue.text: Head of entertainment, facing a charge, moves forward without fear

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, the one that is about to travel
a letter that moves forward advances along the word, leaving its place at the front

parts.note: fun is entertainment
taken as written
a raid is a sudden charge or attack

explanation.surface: A bold entertainment boss presses on despite facing an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests a legal accusation but means an attack. 'Head of entertainment' looks like a job title, yet only the first letter travels, two places along.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unafraid is to show no fright or dread, the plain meaning of acting without fear.

clue.text: Quiet male worker is overwhelming when game

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf completely, so one piece is swallowed inside another

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
he is a male pronoun
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A shy man at work becomes overbearing whenever he is up for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' reads as an adjective meaning willing, but it is the noun for hunted birds. The 'male worker' pair is split open to hold the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheasants are shot for sport and food, so they are a classic example of birds hunted as game.

clue.text: A sweet thing to find precious metal on doorway

parts.note: a gate is an entrance or doorway
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: How lovely to discover gold left on your doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'on' puts the gold after the doorway. 'A sweet thing' sounds like praise for a kind act, but it is a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream cake, so it is a sugary dessert, a sweet thing to eat.

clue.text: Damage for adult in gay magazine

indicators.note: one thing given for another is swapped in its place

parts.note: damage can mean loss, as in 'damage to property'
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
taken as written

explanation.surface: Compensation sought by an adult over something printed in a gay publication.
explanation.walkthrough: GAY swaps its A for LOSS. 'Gay magazine' reads as one phrase, but 'in' separates the wordplay from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy is a magazine printed on shiny paper, typically fashion or celebrity, so the noun names the publication.

clue.text: Picnic's dessert has meat in it

indicators.note: something with an item in it holds that item inside

parts.note: cake is a dessert
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: A picnic pudding that turns out to have meat baked into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picnic's' looks possessive, but the 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A clambake is an American seaside party where shellfish are cooked outdoors, a kind of beach picnic.

clue.text: Explosive stuff stored in Goodison, evacuated after second game

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it

indicators.note: something stored in a place is kept inside it
an evacuated building is emptied, so only the outer letters stay

parts.note: first and last letters
ammo is short for ammunition

explanation.surface: Explosives found hidden at an emptied football stadium after a second match.
explanation.walkthrough: Goodison Park is Everton's football ground in Liverpool. 'Second game' looks like a match number, but 'second' is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game for two players moving counters by dice throws, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Second-hand clothes that woman showed

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it up, so one piece dresses the other

parts.note: second-hand goods are used
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman showing off the thrift-shop outfit she found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun for garments, but it is a verb meaning dresses or wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone is to guide or escort them, as in being shown to your seat.

clue.text: Animated explorer and daughter impressed by band from Birmingham, a place of fabulous wealth

indicators.note: something impressed by another has that thing pressed into it, so it ends up enclosed

parts.note: the Electric Light Orchestra formed in Birmingham
Dora the Explorer is a children's cartoon
D abbreviates daughter

explanation.surface: A cartoon adventurer and her child, wowed by a rock group, find a land of riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressed' suggests admiration, but here it means pressed inside. Birmingham is England's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado is the legendary city of gold sought by Spanish conquistadors, now any place of great riches.

clue.text: See 5
Essential part of sweetcorn, and there's a lot more

indicators.note: the essential part of anything is its core, so the middle letters are taken

parts.note: the central letters, the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A list of vegetables trailing off, with sweetcorn first and plenty more to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of the word gives ETC, which is only the abbreviation; the answer is the full Latin phrase it stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'and the rest', used to show that a list carries on beyond the items named.

clue.text: Expert pop star not being paid

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert
Bono is the singer of U2

explanation.surface: A skilled pop musician playing a benefit gig for no fee.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits Bono's charity work, which makes the split between expert and star easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro bono work, short for pro bono publico, is professional service given free for the public good.

clue.text: Animal moving abroad in both directions

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: left and right, L and R

indicators.note: letters on the move are shifting about, so they change their order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A creature migrating overseas, travelling both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In both directions' looks like a reversal hint, but it means the reshuffled word goes inside L and R, left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labrador retriever is a popular breed of dog, so it is a particular kind of animal.

clue.text: A place where you may get lost endlessly on a river.

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

parts.words: A place where you may get lost
parts.note: a maze is a puzzle of paths built to get lost in
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drifting on a river through a wilderness where you could vanish for good.
explanation.walkthrough: The jungle picture makes 'A place where you may get lost' look like the definition; it is the wordplay, and the river comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon in South America is the largest river on Earth by volume of water.

clue.text: What's left on a cemetery's borders

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
taken as written

indicators.note: the borders of something are its edges, so only the outer letters count

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: Asking what remains of the dead at the edges of a graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the half of the field behind a right-hander's legs is the leg or on side, so 'on' gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is property or money bequeathed in a will, the thing someone has left to heirs.

clue.text: It's spoken in Pakistan, half of Laos and oddly Hungary on top of that

indicators.note: keeping only half of a word means cutting the other half away

parts.note: half of the four letters: the front pair

indicators.note: something arranged oddly is out of its normal order

parts.note: H is Hungary's international vehicle code
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A geography quiz mixing up a language of Pakistan with Laos and Hungary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts you to take the odd letters of HUNGARY; it shuffles 'and' instead. 'Hungary on top of that' places H above the shuffled word in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahnda is a group of Punjabi dialects of western Punjab, a tongue used in parts of Pakistan.

clue.text: Noted German charioteer losing wheel

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter goes missing

parts.note: a wagoner drives a horse-drawn vehicle
O is round, like a wheel

explanation.surface: A famous German chariot racer losing a wheel mid-race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' looks like famous, but it hints at musical notes. A charioteer is loosely a driver of a horse-drawn cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was the German composer of the Ring cycle, so he is a German famous for music.

clue.text: Initially not sure they're collections of 10s

indicators.note: something taken initially is taken at its start, its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of the word
'sure' as a reply means yes

explanation.surface: Someone unsure whether groups of tens count.
explanation.walkthrough: '10s' refers to the answer at 10 across, PHEASANT, not the number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A nye is the old collective noun for a brood or flock of pheasants, so nyes are flocks of those birds.

clue.text: Giant insects, one of them biting Henry

indicators.note: a mouth that bites something closes around it, holding it inside

parts.note: the first of two insects
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
the second insect

explanation.surface: A swarm of huge bugs, one of which has bitten a man called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insects' supplies two of them, BEE and MOTH; 'one of them' is the first, which bites the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A behemoth is a biblical beast and now anything enormous, a noun for a giant.

clue.text: God may be seen as model, I assume

parts.note: to model is to pose
taken as written
to don clothes is to put them on, to assume them

explanation.surface: A model guessing that people might think of them as divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I assume' reads as a hedge, as in 'I suppose', but 'assume' means put on clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek deity of the sea, earthquakes and horses, one of the Olympians.

clue.text: Busy road blocked by enormous delivery

indicators.note: a thing blocked is obstructed by something lodged in its middle
something busy is all activity and bustle, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
OS is outsize, a clothing abbreviation

explanation.surface: A crowded street jammed by a huge lorry dropping off goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests a parcel, but it is a ball bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A doosra is a cricket ball from an off-spinner that turns the opposite way, a deceptive bowled delivery.
